RAIV fleet KPIs

—

From each truck's Apera vision PC log (daily emails, saved to OneDrive). A pick is the robot fetching a new trajectory from Apera. Pick time is the time from one pick to the next while running (gaps under 60 s). "While picking" counts only the time inside pick-and-place sessions, which end at a 5-minute gap or a calibration. Target: 800 picks per hour.

Each truck, all days on record

Where the 800/hr goes

From target to actual picks

While running (all gaps under 30 minutes), every 4.5 s is one pick at 800/hr. Each bar is picks lost to that cause, all days on record. Gaps of 30 minutes or more count as not running and are left out.

Stop time by cause

Minutes in stops of 1 to 30 minutes, all days on record. Cause comes from the Apera and robot logs around each stop: calibration, camera faults, an Apera restart, the robot program being stopped, no plate on the belt, or the robot link dropping.

Every stop of a minute or more

Longest first, for the trucks and days selected above. "Not logged" means neither log shows a cause; those are the stops to ask the crew about.

TruckDateStartEndMinutesCauseEvidenceProgram

Program versions

Which program ran each day

From each robot controller's log. Solid: the log shows the program that day. Faded: no robot log that day, so the last logged program is assumed.

Before and after each change

Each program version's days on record. Lost to stops is the share of running time spent in stops of 1 to 30 minutes. Robot columns come from the robot's own cycle log.

Day by day

Picks per day

Same scale for every truck. Days with the Apera PC on but no picks show as an empty slot.

Pick rate while picking, against the 800/hr target

Filled dot: the day's picks per hour of picking. Ring: its best 10 minutes. Days with fewer than 20 picks are left out.

Part mix

Parts picked against parts seen on the belt

Picked: each pick credited to the part Apera planned it for (its pick point). On belt: what Apera's detector saw in each camera shot. A part is usually seen in several shots, so belt bars show the mix, not unique parts.

Part counts

Shots with part: share of camera shots where Apera saw at least one. Spike picking is switched off in every pipeline; anchor picking is on for 2RT57 and 3RT51.

TruckPartPicked% of picksBelt detections% of beltShots with part

Where pick time goes

Start from the place area or the trigger pose

Median pick time by where the camera captured the next plate. Bar labels give each pose's share of that truck's picks.

Pick time spread

Share of each truck's picks in each half-second band, gaps under 60 s. Anything over 12 s is in the last band.

Vision health

Calibration attempts

Camera calibration is Apera's stereo calibration (error in pixels). Robot calibration is hand-eye (average error X/Y/Z and largest error, mm).

TruckDateStartTypeResultCam px avgAvg X mmAvg Y mmAvg Z mmMax mmNote

Days with camera or robot-link faults

Count of log lines per day. "Camera not found" and "capture failed" mean the camera dropped off; robot link means Apera could not reach the robot.

TruckDateCamera not foundCapture failedCamera linkRobot linkMiscalibrated

Pick quality

Share of Apera's scenes with a pickable plate, per day. The rest found no plate or only unpickable ones. Days under 20 scenes are left out.

Robot controller errors

Error classes in each robot's own log since August, placeholder-clock entries mapped to their real day. Motion-cancelled on stop is left out.

TruckErrorCountFirstLast

Pipeline config changes

Changes to each Apera PC's binpick_pipelines.json, checked every hour. A successful robot calibration also writes this file.

Robot cycle breakdown

Where a cycle goes (median seconds)

From each robot's own per-pick log, every day on record. Top bar: what the arm does each cycle. 2RT57 also logs the next picture, which runs during the place move (bottom bar); when that is longer than the place move, the arm waits.

Robot cycle by day

Median pick, place and waiting-on-vision seconds per day the robot logged at least 20 cycles. The black tick is the median cycle. Dates are on the Apera PC clock.

Robot and Apera, cycle by cycle

Robot cycles matched to an Apera pick within 1.5 s. Robot wait is what the robot logged as waiting on vision; Apera's own count of that is "robot movement blocked". Capture is Apera's picture-taking stage for that pick.
